answer: One concrete defense is requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught double-signing or spamming identities, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Like a meadow that only supports as many grazing herds as its grass can feed, the network caps how many identities one stake can fund, and a reputation graph, a nebula of verified interactions, makes new identities start with zero trust until they earn it through honest work.
